facility_roles.quote: PIONEER is a next-generation rare pion decay experiment, accepted as a high priority experiment at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland.

Demonstrator runs are expected at PSI in late 2026 and TRIUMF in 2027, with physics data taking aimed by the end of the decade.
intervals.quote: The experiment is approved at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI).

name: PIONEER
notes: PSI says the design learns "from the previous generation PEN and PiENu measurements" (PSI page); PIONEER is the planned successor programme but no lineage edge is recorded because a lineage relation needs both sources to say so explicitly.

PIONEER is a collaboration of 80 researchers from 25 universities and national laboratories in Canada, China, Japan, Switzerland and the USA (PSI page); the same demonstrator programme includes a TRIUMF run in 2027.

physics_goals.quote: In Phase I, PIONEER aims to measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs.\ muons $R_{e/\mu}$ to 1 part in $10^4$
physics_goals.value: Measure the charged-pion branching ratio to electrons vs. muons (phase I) and pion beta decay (phases II-III) to test lepton flavour universality and CKM unitarity

summary.plain: A next-generation experiment planned at the Paul Scherrer Institute to measure how often a charged pion decays to an electron rather than a muon, and pion beta decay, to test whether electrons and muons are treated alike. It is approved and in its demonstrator phase.
summary.technical: PIONEER (PSI R-22-01.1): phase I aims at R_e/mu to 1 part in 10^4 (15 times better than current), phases II and III at pion beta decay for V_ud and CKM unitarity; active LGAD target and a 25 X0 3pi sr calorimeter (LXe or LYSO). Approved with high priority; physics data taking aimed by 2030.
